g.text: (a) Tap-path impulse response (as seen by a 10 ns raised-cosine symbol; grid = symbol instants)

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f0efec

g.text: (c) Folded combiner waveforms at layer 1 (not a true eye: multi-level sums; gain-trimmed, model units; same example and output line)

text.style: font-size: 7.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #c3c2b7

g.text: Both channels have the same nominal geometry (RG-58, v_p = 19.8 cm/ns for R). C's SPICE line is a constant-R LTRA

text.style: font-size: 7.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #c3c2b7

g.text: line, so its DC loss is overstated (about -3.6 dB vs -2.2 dB at 100 MHz for the longest layer-1 tap); R is skin-

text.style: font-size: 7.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #c3c2b7

g.text: effect (~sqrt f) loss with 5 % end mismatch (ripple) and a 10 dB coupler / N-way Wilkinson (their fixed gain is

text.style: font-size: 7.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #c3c2b7

g.text: divided out here). The eyes differ in more than the line: C drives trapezoid pulses (1 ns edges) through ideal VCVS

text.style: font-size: 7.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #c3c2b7

g.text: taps, R uses raised-cosine pulses and includes tap amplitude/phase errors, leakage and crosstalk.
